guide: Share a travel app with a read-only demo, a launch page and a feedback loop so investors, tech fans and early users can try it without signing up.
You need: a working web app, a hosting account such as Vercel, a database such as Supabase, and a Product Hunt account.
1. Build the app with ChatGPT (Codex) or Claude Code, hosting it on Vercel with Supabase for the database and sign-in.
1. Create a demo account in Supabase and give it read-only access, using row-level security policies that allow SELECT and block every write.
1. Add a "Try demo account" button on the landing page that signs visitors into that account, so they see the full app without registering.
1. Put your most distinctive feature first in the demo, so it is the first thing a visitor sees.
1. Prepare a Product Hunt launch page with a short tagline, screenshots, a demo link and a clear first comment explaining who it is for.
1. Publish the page, then share the link in short videos or posts aimed at technology fans and people interested in investing.
1. Collect feedback from comments and messages, note what people liked, and fix what they mention before the next update.
Watch out: Give the demo account read access only, and test that it cannot edit or delete anything, otherwise visitors can change real data.

```
You are helping me set up a safe public demo and a Product Hunt launch for my web app. The app is <describe your app in one sentence>. It is hosted on <Vercel or other host> and uses <Supabase or other database> for data and sign-in.
Please do the following:
1. Create a demo user and write row-level security policies so that this user can read the data needed to show <your standout feature> but cannot insert, update or delete anything.
2. Add a "Try demo account" button to the landing page that signs visitors into the demo user without asking for an email or password.
3. Write tests that confirm the demo user is blocked from every write action.
4. Draft the Product Hunt listing: a tagline under 60 characters, a description of about 250 words for <target audience>, a list of screenshots to capture, and a first comment from the maker.
Constraints: do not expose service keys in the browser, keep the demo data free of real customer information, and explain each change in plain English.
Return the code changes, the SQL policies, the test results and the Product Hunt text.
```
